records.title: A finished, telomere-to-telomere assembly for  Botrytis cinerea  strain B05.10
records.abstract: We present an improved genome assembly of Botrytis cinerea strain B05.10 which serves as a reference isolate for most labs active in the Botrytis research. The existing assembly dating from 2017 was extended by adding 8 telomeric regions and a small number of minor errors was corrected. The new assembly contains telomeres on each chromosome end, except for Chr4 carrying the rDNA repeat. The unannotated assembly is deposited in NCBI and manual curation of gene models is ongoing. The new assembly will be hosted on Ensembl-Fungi after completion of the structural curation.
records.authors: van Kan JA, Zheng D, Pieterse FP, Shi-Kunne X.

records.title: Exogenous granular activated carbon (GAC) promotes the biogenic oxidative dissolution of rhodochrosite and the degradation of pollutants: Insights from extracellular superoxide radical generation, key enzyme activities and transcriptomic analysis.
records.abstract: The oxidative dissolution of rhodochrosite (MnCO3) affects the availability of divalent Mn(II) ions and regulates the content of manganese oxides in aquatic environments; however, the effects of exogenous particles on the bacterial oxidation of rhodochrosite and the degradation of pollutants have not been elucidated. In this study, the underlying molecular mechanisms of the bacterial oxidative dissolution of rhodochrosite in the presence of granular active carbon (GAC) were investigated. After 120 h of reaction, the concentration of biogenic MnO2in situ-generated reached 24.76 mg/L in the MnCO3@GAC system, which was significantly greater than the concentrations observed in the treatments with pure MnCO3 (18.43 mg/L) and dissolved Mn(II) (10.50 mg/L) (p 3@GAC system. The biogenic oxidation of MnCO3@GAC resulted in excellent degradation efficiency for phenylarsonic acid (PAA). The degradation efficiency of PAA was significantly greater than those of the MnCO3 and MnB1 treatments, which could efficiently remove 92.5% PAA. These findings provide new insights into the biogeochemical cycles of rhodochrosite.

records.title: Protein structural changes, volatile flavor evolution and microbial community succession in Opsariichthys bidens during simulated natural refrigerated transport: a correlation analysis.
records.abstract: Chinese hook snout carp (Opsariichthys bidens) deteriorates readily during postharvest transport, yet the interplay between muscle protein degradation, volatile flavor formation, and microbial metabolism under realistic transportation conditions remains poorly understood. This is the first study to systematically investigate the correlation between protein structural changes and microbial metabolism in Chinese hook snout carp during refrigerated transport simulating natural conditions at 4 °C, 16 °C, and 32 °C. Elevated temperatures accelerate myofibrillar protein denaturation. Compared with fresh samples, α-helix content decreases by approximately 8.5% under 32 °C for 24 h, while random coil content increases by 12.3%, accompanied by reduced water-holding capacity (moisture content declining from 81.64% to 74.92%). Flavor profiles are dominated by aldehydes at 4 °C, whereas sulfur compounds, indole, and pyridines gradually accumulate with rising temperature, and severe flavor deterioration occurs within only 12 h at 32 °C. Low-temperatures enriched psychrotrophic Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas, whereas elevated temperatures promoted diverse mesophilic spoilage bacteria with enhanced amino acid, lipid, and carbohydrate metabolism. Transport temperature serves as the primary driver of quality loss, with storage duration exerting cumulative amplification effects. Our findings provide correlation-based insights into temperature-dependent quality deterioration that can inform cold-chain optimization strategies.
records.authors: Wang J, Xu L, Ying X, Deng S, Yu J, Weng X, Sartoni M, Guidi A, Zhang J.

records.title: Combined effects of microplastics and petroleum hydrocarbons on Chlorella vulgaris in different aquatic ecosystems: Bioavailability study.
records.abstract: Microplastics (MPs), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPHs) frequently coexist in aquatic ecosystems, creating complex pollution scenarios whose interaction with primary producers remains poorly understood. This study evaluates, for the first time, how extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) secreted by Chlorella vulgaris modulate interactions between polyethylene microplastics (PE-MPs) and mixtures of PAHs-TPHs across salinity gradients, and how these processes influence the physiological responses of the microalgae. Using a 23 factorial design, EPS production and characterization were analyzed using FTIR, PAHs-TPHs removal, aggregate formation, chlorophyll, and growth. The growth of C. vulgaris increased in freshwater and marine water by 36.7% and 57.4%, respectively. In brackish water, however, it was inhibited by up to 80%. Chlorophyll decreased significantly in brackish water as PE-MP concentrations increased. EPS varied according to salinity and pollutant load, reaching a maximum of 54.5 μg mL-1 in marine water and being positively associated with PAHs-TPHs removal. Under conditions of high salinity or high pollutant load, the decrease in EPS coincided with lower removal and growth inhibition. FTIR analyses showed changes in the functional composition of EPS, and SEM images confirmed the formation of microalgae-EPS-MPs (MEM) aggregates. This work demonstrates that C. vulgaris modulates interactions between PE-MPs and PAHs/TPHs mixtures through EPS, which act as key interfacial mediators that regulate the bioavailability and fate of these pollutants in aquatic systems, providing essential knowledge for the advancement of microalgae-based strategies for the treatment of emerging pollutants.
records.authors: Gomez CLG, Ramirez KDR, Ñañez KB, Marques IM, Moreira ÍTA.

records.title: Evaluation of genomic prediction accuracy for yield-related traits in Pyropia haitanensis.
records.abstract: Pyropia haitanensis, a representative species of intertidal red algae, has significant economic value. However, its traditional breeding cycle is lengthy and inefficient, leading to a shortage of new varieties of P. haitanensis. Genomic selection (GS), an efficient molecular-breeding strategy, holds promise for accelerating the genetic improvement of yield-related traits. To date, no systematic GS study has been reported for red algae. In this study, we used a doubled haploid (DH) population to perform genomic prediction for five yield‑related traits (length, width, fresh weight, days to maturity, and thickness) based on whole-genome sequencing data. We systematically compared the effects of eight statistical models on prediction accuracy and evaluated the effect of different marker densities, ranging from 100 SNPs to the full marker set, under two SNP selection strategies: genome-wide association study (GWAS)-based selection and random selection. The results showed that the heritability of five yield traits ranged from 0.12 (length) to 0.57 (thickness). The random forest (RF) model consistently achieved higher prediction accuracy than the other models across all traits, with accuracies ranging from 0.448 for length to 0.727 for thickness. For all models, prediction accuracy reached a plateau when the number of markers was in the range of 1,000-5,000, with limited gains from further increases in marker density. GWAS-based selection performed better than random selection for most traits at low marker densities (100-1,000 SNPs), while random selection showed higher accuracy for width. In summary, the application of genomic selection of P. haitanensis breeding provides an effective strategy for identifying superior candidate individuals. In practical applications, the optimal model should be selected flexibly according to the genetic architecture of the traits and the available SNP density.Supplementary informationThe online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s11032-026-01732-y.
records.journal: Molecular breeding : new strategies in plant improvement
records.authors: Wang J, Kong L, Xu Y, Ji D, Xie C, Wang W.

records.title: Evidence of direct iron delivery by ABCI10 to DJA5/6 for chloroplast Fe-S cluster biogenesis.
records.abstract: Iron-sulfur (Fe-S) clusters are among the oldest cofactors in biology, required for electron transfer, catalysis and regulatory switching. Consequently, chloroplasts harbor numerous Fe-S protein-dependent processes, ranging from photosynthesis to metabolism. The assembly and transfer reactions of chloroplast Fe-S cluster biogenesis are increasingly well defined, yet how iron reaches the assembly machinery has remained unresolved. Previous studies have demonstrated that the DnaJ proteins DJA5 and DJA6 can bind iron and directly facilitate its incorporation into SUFBC2D, the scaffold for Fe-S assembly in chloroplasts. Yet, the source of iron for DJA5/6 remains unknown. Here, we show that impairing the chloroplast inner membrane iron transporter PERMEASE IN CHLOROPLASTS 1 (PIC1) does not appreciably affect SUFB and SUFC content, whereas mutating ABCI10, a subunit of a prokaryotic-type energy coupling factor (ECF) transporter, reduces the abundance of SUFB and SUFC. This indicates that ABCI10 is required for the abundance of the SUFBC2D complex, consistent with the requirement for DJA5/6 in maintaining SUFBC2D content. Bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) and yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) assays further show that ABCI10 interacts with DJA5/6, but not with ABCI12. Taken together, we propose that ABCI10, a subunit of the prokaryotic-type ECF transporter, contributes to the iron supply required by SUFBC2D and is spatially positioned to deliver iron to DJA5/6 for Fe-S biosynthesis in chloroplasts, whereas PIC1 is not the major iron donor for this pathway.
records.authors: Jia T, Yang B, Cheng Y, Wu T, Hu X.

records.title: Genomic Data Reveals Key Candidate Genes Underlying Chicken Comb Morphology.
records.abstract: Comb morphology is a salient chicken trait of biological and breeding interest. We analyzed whole-genome data from 228 birds representing 10 breeds, including Hetian (HTC) and Xiangdong (XDC)-the only two Chinese breeds with carnation combs-to investigate population structure, diversity, and genomic correlates of comb type. Population analyses revealed clear breed stratification, with clustering that partly tracked comb type; breeds subjected to strong artificial selection or bottlenecks showed reduced genetic diversity. The integrated fixation index (F ST) and genome-wide association study (GWAS) approach highlighted multiple regions differentiating carnation- from non-carnation-comb birds, with the strongest, most consistent signal at HSF5. Additional associated loci included EDN3, ITGB8, PDE4B, SDK1, MC1R, CDKL5, NRXN1, and STAG3. Gene-set enrichment pointed to pathways involved in vascular development and embryogenesis, processes plausibly contributing to comb morphogenesis. Notably, while HTC and XDC maintained distinct global genomic backgrounds, they exhibited high similarity within the major candidate genes influencing the carnation comb phenotype, suggesting that independent breed differentiation occurred alongside a shared genetic basis for this trait. While causative variants were not established, these results nominate tractable candidates and pathways for functional validation and inform marker development for conservation and selection in indigenous breeds.

records.title: Molecular epidemiology of carbapenemase producing Enterobacterales; insights into microbial diversity and transmission in the mid-west of Ireland.
records.abstract: BackgroundThe World Health Organization recognises Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) as a global health security threat. The aim of this study is to review the molecular epidemiology of CPE in the mid-west of Ireland over a four-year period (2018 - 2022) with characterisation of CPE strains causing clusters.MethodsA retrospective genomic and clinical surveillance study was undertaken of CPE isolates from patient and environmental sources.Results426 patients yielded 542 CPE organisms; 255 (60%) were male. Isolates from screening samples predominated (504/542, 92%). 412 (96.7%) patients were from acute settings. 114 (23.4%) were known CPE contacts before detection. Citrobacter freundii complex prevalence was highest (151/542, 28%) followed by Escherichia coli (120/542, 22%). Ten carbapenemase genes were identified; blaOXA-48 (n=221) became the most prevalent by the end of the study period in comparison to a higher prevalence of blaKPC-2 (n= 315) for the first three years. 47 environmental isolates were also studied; Citrobacter freundii complex blaKPC-2 predominated again (31/47, n=66%). The genetic background of Citrobacter species and E. coli was highly diverse with ST 420 and ST38 being the predominant sequence types, respectively. Several cluster codes were assigned, suggestive of putative transmission events between patients and their environment.ConclusionIn the context of new CPE detections per 10,000 admissions increasing from 5.275 in 2018 to 15.863 in 2022, ongoing screening, coupled to clinical and genomic surveillance are essential to control their spread.
records.authors: O'Connell NH, Powell J, Kiely P, Dunne CP.

records.title: Recovery of a CMV-Reactive TCR From a Clinical Virus-Specific T-Cell Product for Generation of a Defined TCR-T Cell Product.
records.abstract: Virus-specific T-cell (VST) therapy is used in the management of viral complications after allogeneic HSCT. Current VST products are polyclonal and heterogeneous. This limits standardization, potency assessment, and precise product characterization. T-cell receptor (TCR)-based engineering may allow antiviral specificity to be captured from donor-derived immunity and redirected into a more defined cellular therapy candidate. To identify a functional cytomegalovirus (CMV)-reactive TCR from a donor-derived VST product administered to a patient, generate and characterize a defined anti-CMV TCR-T cell candidate, and assess TRAC knockout as a strategy to support endogenous TCR removal in future allogeneic applications. A trivalent donor-derived VST product generated against adenovirus, BK polyomavirus, and CMV was administered under compassionate use to a pediatric haploidentical HSCT recipient with post-transplant viremia. Serial post-infusion blood samples were used to assess changes in the peripheral T-cell receptor repertoire over time. The clinical VST product was re-stimulated with the human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-A*02:01-restricted CMV pp65 495-503 epitope. Antigen-responsive CD8⁺4-1BB⁺ cultures were used for functional TCR recovery. The selected CMV-reactive TCR was reconstructed with murine constant regions, cloned into an MSGV1 gamma-retroviral vector, and introduced into primary human T cells. Engineered cells were assessed for introduced TCR expression, antigen-specific activation, interferon-gamma (IFNγ) secretion, HLA-A*02:01-restricted recognition, endogenous TCR expression over time, and generation of a TRAC-disrupted TCR-T cell population. Peripheral TCR repertoire analysis after sequential VST infusions showed temporal changes in dominant circulating TCRβ clonotypes, with annotation based on overlap with antigen-responsive CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ reference datasets generated from the clinical VST product. Functional re-stimulation of the VST product with pp65 495-503 enriched antigen-responsive CD8⁺4-1BB⁺ cells. From these cultures, a CMV-reactive TCR was recovered and advanced based on reproducible peptide-specific activity. Following reconstruction and retroviral transfer, the selected TCR mediated pp65 495-503-specific activation and IFNγ secretion in primary T cells. Stimulation with pp65 495-503 induced 35.82% CD3⁺OX40⁺4-1BB⁺ cells and approximately 9.8 × 10³ pg/mL IFNγ, while responses to non-cognate adenoviral Hexon stimulation remained low. The engineered anti-CMV TCR-T cells showed stronger IFNγ responses to pp65 495-503 than the parental VST product. Irrelevant TCR controls remained near baseline. Endogenous TCR expression decreased early after TCR transduction alone but recovered by approximately day 14 and persisted through day 35. Following CRISPR/Cas9-mediated TRAC knockout, approximately 70% of cells were within the intended mTCR⁺hTCR⁻ population before sorting, and this population was enriched by flow sorting for downstream characterization. This study demonstrates a clinically grounded workflow for deriving a defined antiviral TCR-T cell candidate from a donor-derived VST product. A functional CMV-reactive TCR was recovered from the clinical VST product and redirected into primary T cells while preserving pp65-specific activity. The recovery of endogenous TCR expression after transduction alone indicates that early downmodulation is not sufficient for durable removal of the native TCR. Incorporating TRAC knockout therefore provides a strategy to generate a more defined engineered T-cell population for future antiviral cellular therapy development.

records.title: Native AMF from wild Paeonia ostii enhance root development via PoCCD4-mediated hormone homeostasis and reshape rhizosphere microbiome assembly and function.
records.abstract: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) play vital roles in plant growth and rhizosphere microbiome assembly. Tree peony (Paeonia sect. Moutan DC.) is an economically valuable perennial crop, yet the symbiotic mechanisms between it and native AMF remain poorly understood. In this study, we surveyed the rhizosphere AMF community of wild P. ostii from its native habitat, and isolated two dominant species: Funneliformis mosseae and Claroideoglomus etunicatum. Inoculation with these AMF significantly improved root development and leaf photosynthetic efficiency. Furthermore, the promotion involved a novel pathway whereby carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 4 (PoCCD4) mediated strigolactone and abscisic acid homeostasis in P. ostii roots. Beyond direct effects on host plant growth, AMF inoculation fine-tuned rhizosphere microbiota composition, reinforcing host-driven assembly and favoring beneficial consortia without altering overall diversity. Correlation analyses revealed that the AMF-shaped microenvironment established a disease-suppressive network linked to soil nutrient dynamics and phytohormone profiles. This study elucidates the interaction mechanisms between native AMF and P. ostii, uncovers their co-adaptive relationships, and offers a scientific basis for developing AMF inoculants for sustainable tree peony cultivation.
records.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology

records.title: Non-viral delivery and genome editing for CAR-NK engineering in solid tumors: from ex vivo manufacturing to in vivo reprogramming.
records.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-engineered natural killer (NK) cell therapy has emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy for cancer treatment, offering advantages over CAR-T cells such as a lower risk of cytokine release syndrome and graft-versus-host disease and the potential for off-the-shelf manufacturing. Viral vectors have long served as effective tools for CAR-NK engineering, but their dependence on complex manufacturing procedures, considerable production costs, and the potential risks associated with genomic integration has encouraged increasing interest in non-viral alternatives. Recent advances in genetic engineering technologies have facilitated the development of CAR-NK platforms, particularly through non-viral delivery approaches including electroporation, transposon systems and lipid nanoparticles, while CRISPR-based tools enable targeted genome editing. Meanwhile, an increasing number of clinical trials have begun to evaluate the safety and therapeutic potential of CAR-NK cells in both hematological malignancies and solid tumors. However, challenges such as limited NK-cell persistence, antigen heterogeneity, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment remain. In this review, we summarize recent progress in non-viral CAR-NK engineering strategies, analyze the current landscape of preclinical and clinical trials, and discuss key challenges and future directions for advancing CAR-NK therapy. Collectively, these advances suggest that non-viral engineering technologies may serve as an important technological foundation for next-generation CAR-NK therapies, enabling more flexible ex vivo manufacturing and potentially supporting the future development of in vivo CAR-NK generation strategies for solid tumors.
records.authors: Shen Y, Ye X, Shen S, Lv F.

records.title: S-layers as functional armours: structure, function and variability in Clostridioides difficile.
records.abstract: Surface layers (S-layers) are paracrystalline protein lattices that serve as molecular exoskeletons and environmental interfaces across diverse bacteria and archaea. Despite their widespread occurrence, S-layers remain comparatively understudied. The available models do not fully represent the structural and physiological diversity of S-layers, and fragmented methodologies limit comprehensive functional comparisons and detailed characterisation. Recently determined high-resolution structural details for multiple variants of Clostridioides difficile S-layer provide a uniquely rich model system with functional links to antimicrobial resistance, phage recognition and immune evasion. In this review, we present C. difficile S-layers as extremely diverse, adaptable and multifunctional structures. We (i) summarise known S-layer roles in C. difficile infection; (ii) present a comprehensive comparison of their extremely diverse structures, including unique features and topological differences in lattice assemblies; (iii) propose quantitative metrics for comparative, structural analysis of these S-layers; (iv) outline S-layer pore size thresholds for the diffusion of metabolites essential for C. difficile growth; and (v) explore possible mechanisms underlying S-layer function and highlight the key outstanding questions.
records.authors: Salgado PS, Sendra KM, Barwinska-Sendra A.

records.title: A bistable type III secretion system is primed and loaded in  Pseudomonas aeruginosa  hypervirulent isolates with positively selected codon changes in  exsA  or  exsD
records.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa has multiple virulence factors that promote airway infections in people with immune deficiencies. Most clinical isolates from human infections have functional type III secretion systems (T3SSs) that are subject to bistable regulation and secrete the cytotoxic effector ExoS into neutrophils. During airway infection in people with cystic fibrosis (CF),  P. aeruginosa maintains bistable regulation or genetically adapts by inactivating or hyperactivating T3SS expression. CF clinical isolates with hyperactive T3SSs have codon changes in the transcriptional regulators,  exsA or  exsD. It is not known how these mutations: 1) arise, 2) promote hypervirulence, or 3) impact bistable T3SS regulation. To understand how these mutants arise, ∼24,000 genomes in the NCBI Pathogens database were searched for positively selected mutations in  exs genes based on nonsynonomous to synonymous codon change ratios. Missense and nonsense mutations were detected in  exsA (47) or  exsD (45) the majority of which are predicted to be positively selected. To determine how one of these codon changes promotes hypervirulence, an  exsA T48I isolate was used to establish lung infections in mice engineered with a CF genotype. The  exsA T48I mutant and an  exsA + control had similar lung burdens, but the former caused exacerbated weight loss and lung inflammation, suggesting immunopathology from phagocyte death as the cause of hypervirulence. Two additional hyperactive mutants were identified by screening a small collection of isolates from children with CF. Immunoblotting and fluorescence microscopy showed that hyperactive  exsA or  exsD mutants increased production of T3SS injectisomes and effectors, indicating they have “primed and loaded” phenotypes. ExsA dimer modeling revealed that codon changes like T48I in the β-barrel domain cause a conformational change that hyperactivates the transcription factor. These results define that hyperactive mutants are positively selected, hypervirulent due to lung inflammation, and have primed and loaded T3SSs.
records.authors: Reuven AD, Katzenell S, Rapp AW, Oates JC, Pennington JP, Hampton TH, Bomberger JM, Cherry JL, Bliska JB.

records.title: Comparative analysis identifies a shared topological organisation among divergent arenavirus intergenic RNAs
records.abstract: ABSTRACT  Biological function is often inferred from sequence conservation or structural similarity. However, many viral RNAs maintain regulatory functions despite extensive diversification of both sequence and structures. Using arenavirus intergenic regions (IGRs) as a model system, we investigated what level of RNA organization remains conserved when these conventional sequence-structure-function relationships break down. Combining cryogenic OrbiSIMS guided RNA structure determination with graph theory-based analysis of fifty-eight IGRs across phylogenetically diverse arenaviruses, we discovered that IGR topology, defined by the connectivity and relative integration of individual stem-loop elements, is consistently arranged around a highly connected helical core that persists across divergent IGR folds. Quantitative centrality analyses further revealed that topologically peripheral stem-loops are comparatively sparse and variable across the phylogenetic classes. Investigation of the functional consequence of the peripheral elements in Golden Gate virus (a reptile arenavirus) S-IGR revealed selective association with interferon-induced and antiviral RNA-binding proteins in human host cells infected with recombinant Lymphocytic Choriomeningitis virus (a distantly related human arenavirus). Taken together, these findings identify graph-defined topology as a recurrent organisational feature among divergent arenavirus IGRs that is not captured by sequence identity or global RNA-structure similarity. The data are consistent with a model in which a topologically central helical organisation may be associated with conserved regulatory capacity, whereas structurally variable peripheral elements may contribute to lineage- or segment-specific host-factor interaction profiles.
records.authors: Childs A, Ly DTK, Marinus T, Bhosale RA, Daly JM, Tych K, Foster TL, Borkar AN.

records.title: Synthetic biology for heritable viral disease resistance in livestock.
records.abstract: Synthetic biology is rapidly expanding the strategies available to engineer disease resistance in livestock. Genome editing of host factors required for pathogen entry or replication has generated complete or partial resistance in pigs, cattle, and chickens, culminating in the first regulatory approvals of PRRSV-resistant pigs. Another frontier is emerging in which synthetic antiviral circuits detect and suppress infection through programmable molecular responses. Precision editing tools, including base and prime editors, may enable resistance through smaller and more targeted genomic changes, while organoid and stem cell-derived cell cultures are accelerating pre-animal validation. This review examines recent advances in host-factor engineering, synthetic antiviral systems, and enabling platforms, and considers the challenges of commercial dissemination, regulation, and public acceptance. Together, these developments position engineered resistance as a potentially important component of integrated livestock disease control.
records.authors: Beaton BP, Rice E.

records.title: High prevalence of TROP2 expression identifies EBV-positive gastric cancer as a candidate for TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugates.
records.abstract: PurposeTrophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2) is a glycoprotein expressed on epithelial tumor cells and therefore an established target for antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-positive gastric cancer is a molecularly distinct subtype characterized by unique immunological features, including frequent responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Nevertheless, a subset of these patients fails to benefit from ICI therapy, leaving an unmet need for non-immunotherapeutic treatment options. Tumors lacking TROP2, fail to respond to TROP2-directed ADCs. We therefore assessed the prevalence of TROP2 expression in gastric cancer including the EBV-positive subtype, which has not been characterized to date.MethodsTROP2 expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry in 525 patients with gastric cancer classified according to TCGA molecular subtypes, representing the largest Caucasian cohort assessed for TROP2 to date.ResultsTROP2 expression differed significantly across molecular subtypes (p ConclusionNearly all EBV-positive gastric cancers therefore express TROP2 at levels compatible with ADC targeting. These findings identify TROP2 as a target in EBV-positive gastric cancer and provide a rationale for clinical investigation of TROP2-directed ADCs in this molecularly defined population, particularly as a non-immunotherapeutic option for patients who fail ICI therapy.

records.title: Bacillomycin D as a membrane-active scaffold for antifungal and biocontrol applications: chemistry, biosynthesis, mechanisms, and translational readiness.
records.abstract: Bacillomycin D is a membrane-active cyclic lipoheptapeptide of the iturin family produced by Bacillus subtilis, Bacillus amyloliquefaciens and Bacillus velezensis. It is distinguished by a β-amino fatty acid chain and a cyclic peptide core and shows broad antifungal activity against phytopathogenic and clinically relevant fungi. Its primary action involves membrane disruption, causing ion leakage, membrane depolarisation and cell death, while reactive oxygen species accumulation and anti-biofilm effects may contribute to specific contexts. Biosynthesis is mediated by a hybrid polyketide synthase/nonribosomal peptide synthetase assembly line encoded by the bmy operon and its bam homologues, with production modulated by global transcriptional regulators, including CodY, ComA, DegU and Spo0A. Recent advances in fermentation optimisation, fed-batch production, cell immobilisation and genetic engineering have improved production potential. Nevertheless, translation remains constrained by incomplete homologue-specific activity and toxicity data, limited in vivo validation, scalable manufacturing challenges and insufficient safety assessment. The available patent-screening records indicate technological interest in strain development, fermentation optimisation and antimicrobial applications. This review evaluates the structure, biosynthesis, regulation, production, purification, mechanisms, bioactivity, translational challenges and intellectual property landscape of bacillomycin D.
records.authors: Li HY, Erriah P, Oslan SN, Wan Ahmad Kamil WNI, Sabri S.

records.title: Quantitative diatom analysis for drowning-site determination: Evaluation of accuracy and a practical decision guide.
records.abstract: Thirty-two aquatic-lung pairs from confirmed drowning cases were compared using quantitative exploration of diatom data gathered by the lossless HNO3-PCF extraction method. Permutational analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) demonstrated that aquatic-lung pairs share a highly significant, pair-specific diatom signal (R2 = 0.86, p = 0.001), while differences between aquatic and lung samples remained insignificant, establishing lung samples as highly representative of the site-specific aquatic community. Beta regression analysis proved that the quality of geographical aquatic-lung matching (site spatial tightness) was the sole significant factor affecting pairing accuracy (pseudo-R2 = 0.50), confirming the strong site-specific character of these pairs. In real forensic scenarios where one lung was compared to several aquatic samples, the mutual nearest neighbour (MNN) criterion revealed that pairing accuracy reached 95% for two aquatic samples, maintaining an accuracy of 79% when the candidate pool increased to eleven. To control false positives, the nearest neighbour distance ratio (NNDR) was introduced as the decision parameter. Empirical NNDR 95% thresholds were calibrated to limit the false-positive rate to 5% within the resampling framework (with corresponding true-positive sensitivity reported for the three best-performing quantitative distance metrics: Bray-Curtis, quantitative Jaccard, and Hellinger). Based on these findings, a practical decision guide was developed to enable both the selection of the most probable drowning site and the assessment of match distinctiveness relative to the candidate pool. Our results suggest that quantitative analysis based on sample distance metrics provides a robust, statistically quantifiable framework for drowning-site determination in cases where the true drowning site is present in the candidate pool. However, rejecting false pairings when the true site is absent remains beyond the sensitivity of the method.

records.title: Hypervirulent Listeria isolated from a wild rabbit in Canada.
records.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is the causative agent of listeriosis, a major foodborne disease with a 30% mortality rate in humans. Although L. monocytogenes can infect animals, whether wildlife can serve as a reservoir remains understudied, especially in Canada. Here, we characterized an L. monocytogenes strain (W0463-24) extracted from a wild cottontail rabbit (Sylvilagus floridanus) submitted to the Canadian Wildlife Health Cooperative at the University of Guelph. The rabbit had severe swelling of the head, multiple scabs around the muzzle and eyes, and was diagnosed with disseminated lymphoma, multifocal necrotizing hepatitis with gram-positive bacteria, and nematodosis. Liver and spleen were PCR-negative for Francisella tularensis, and liver was 4+ for L. monocytogenes on bacterial culture. Whole-genome analysis characterized isolate W0463-24 as sequence type 1 (ST1), clonal complex 1 (CC1), and lineage I. Multiple virulence and stress response genes were identified in silico, including the Listeria pathogenicity island 3 (LIPI-3). Invasion of human colon adenocarcinoma (Caco-2) cells in vitro was significantly greater with W0463-24 compared with wild-type strain 10403S. We found that this ST1, CC1, lineage I wildlife isolate has high pathogenic potential, emphasizing wildlife both as potential reservoirs and as populations vulnerable to L. monocytogenes infection.
records.journal: Journal of veterinary diagnostic investigation : official publication of the American Association of Veterinary Laboratory Diagnosticians, Inc
records.authors: Widjaja AF, Jardine CM, Stevens B, Theijn C, Slavic D, Guariglia-Oropeza V.

records.title: Integrative reanalysis of public intracellular and vaccine-challenge transcriptomes, informed by single-cell and metabolomic atlases, refines antigen prioritisation for next-generation veterinary  Brucella  vaccines
records.abstract: Brucellosis is the most widespread bacterial zoonosis and a leading cause of abortion and infertility in cattle, sheep, goats and pigs. The live vaccines licensed for livestock (  B. abortus S19 and RB51,  B. melitensis Rev.1) give incomplete protection, retain residual virulence and induce antibodies that are indistinguishable from those of field infection, and no human vaccine is licensed. Antigen discovery for safer subunit and mRNA alternatives has proceeded one candidate at a time, so it remains unclear which immunogenic proteins are abundant in the intracellular niche that protective immunity must recognise. We reanalysed four public data layers: dual RNA-sequencing of intracellular  B. abortus and infected murine macrophages (GSE100914), splenic transcriptomes from vaccinated and challenged mice (GSE254248), and single-cell (PRJCA054635) and metabolomic (ST003696, ST003692) atlases. Intracellular residence induced 704 genes and repressed 249, enriching translation functions 2.9-fold. Omp28/BP26 was the second most abundant intracellular transcript (35,652 TPM; log2FC 4.25), whereas the lipoproteins omp16, omp10 and omp19 were 116-637-fold less abundant. Vaccination left a germinal-centre and TCF1+ memory imprint rather than an effector-cytokine signature. A composite score combining abundance, induction and surface exposure reorders the candidate panel, placing Omp28/BP26 and omp2b above current candidates and defining concrete priorities for veterinary vaccine development.  Simple Summary  Brucellosis is a bacterial infection that causes abortions, stillbirths and infertility in cattle, sheep, goats and pigs, and it can also pass to people through unpasteurised milk or direct contact with infected animals. Vaccination is the main control measure, but the live vaccines used in livestock do not fully protect animals and make vaccinated animals look infected in the blood tests on which eradication programmes depend. Safer subunit and mRNA vaccines therefore need better target proteins, yet candidates have usually been chosen one at a time from laboratory-grown bacteria, which may not reflect what the bacteria produce inside the animal’s own cells. We reanalysed publicly available datasets that measure gene activity in infected cells and in vaccinated animals. The proteins currently favoured by vaccine developers turn out to be scarce inside host cells, whereas two surface proteins are abundant and strongly switched on. Our ranking, together with the immune features that distinguish protected animals, gives concrete priorities for the next generation of veterinary brucellosis vaccines.
records.authors: Zhao Y, Cheng H, Zhou S, He L, Xiu C, Huang B, Lu X.

records.title: Functional analysis of NANOS protein variants identified in men with infertility employing zebrafish embryos
records.abstract: Study question  Are vertebrate NANOS proteins associated with human fertility, and can a rapid  in vivo assay in zebrafish be established to evaluate the biological activity of human  NANOS variants?  Summary answer  Combining a rapid  in vivo assay we developed for Nanos protein activity and patient-derived genetic data, we identified  NANOS variants that could contribute to male infertility.  What is known already  Male infertility affects approximately 17% of the population, but linking specific gene variants to this condition remains challenging. NANOS proteins are essential regulators of germ cell development in different model organisms; however, a rapid and robust  in vivo assay for evaluating their activity in the context of human male infertility is currently lacking.  Study design, size, duration  Exome/genome data from 3,338 men included in the Male Reproductive Genomics (MERGE) cohort were examined in this study. Of these, 2038 men showed severely impaired spermatogenesis but were otherwise healthy. Ninety-Six men with intact spermatogenesis were included in the study as controls. Additionally, the study included a targeted analysis of  NANOS variants in 44 patients from the IMIGC cohort.  Participants/materials, setting, methods  The exome/genome data were screened for rare, stop-gain, frameshift, splice site, as well as missense variants in  NANOS1 ,  NANOS2 , and  NANOS3 . Human amino acid substitutions were introduced at the corresponding positions in the zebrafish proteins. Ectopic co-expression of wild-type Dnd1 and Nanos3 in zebrafish embryos induces a germ cell-like fate in somatic cells, resulting in severe developmental defects and embryonic lethality. Based on this principle, we established a rapid  in vivo assay in which wild-type Dnd1 was co-expressed with wild-type or variant Nanos2 and Nanos3 proteins in live zebrafish embryos, expecting early embryonic death if a variant protein is functional. This assay was used to evaluate the activity of  NANOS2 and  NANOS3 variants identified in men with infertility.  Main results and the role of chance  In human exome/genome sequencing data, we identified one heterozygous missense variant in NANOS2 and two heterozygous missense variants in NANOS3. The function of the variants was examined in the zebrafish using the  in vivo assay we developed. Co-expression of wild-type Dnd1 with selected Nanos2 or Nanos3 variants identified in infertile men resulted in defects in induction of the germ cell-like phenotype, demonstrating the power of the biological readout for evaluating the potential effects of patient-derived variants on NANOS protein activity. Together, our analysis enabled the evaluation of single nucleotide variants, whose impact on protein function is difficult to predict, and allowed us to distinguish variants with little or no effect on protein function from those that strongly reduce activity and may potentially contribute to infertility.  Limitations, reasons for caution  The assay requires access to zebrafish embryos and basic imaging equipment. Although the functional conservation of NANOS proteins between zebrafish and humans is supported by previous studies, species-specific differences may influence protein activity. Therefore, the zebrafish assay should be considered one component of a broader framework for evaluating  NANOS variants as contributing factor for infertility.  Wider implications of the findings  Using  NANOS2 and  NANOS3 as examples, we demonstrate that integrating clinical genetic data with functional cell and developmental biology can help establish links between candidate disease genes and human fertility. This strategy may apply to other germline-specific genes whose ectopic expression produces measurable developmental phenotypes in zebrafish embryos. (RA 863/17-1, RA 863/18-1), to E.R., C.F., and F.T. (Clinical Research Unit ‘Male Germ Cells’, CRU 326, project number 329621271), to S.K., C.F., and F.T. (Collaborative Research Centre ‘Reproduction.MS’, SFB 1748, project number 549467913), the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) Junior Scientist Research Centre ‘ReproTrack.MS’ to S.K. and F.T. (project number 01GR2303), and funding from the Medical Faculty of the University of Münster. The authors declare no competing interests Trial registration number  N/A.
